title: QBR Metric Decoder - latency, cost-per-token, uptime & cache mapping
content:
Purpose:
This compact reference turns infra/observability metrics (latency, uptime, cost/token, cache-hit) into QBR-friendly KPIs and renewal signals. It is intentionally concise — designed for CS AEs and customer-facing reviews. Use as a checklist + scoring heuristic during monthly run-ups and quarterly business reviews.

Summary mapping (quick):
- Latency (p95 request-to-first-token): customer experience proxy — maps to user-facing responsiveness and cancellation risk.
- Uptime (customer-only uptime; successful inference responses / total requests): reliability baseline; direct SLA translation.
- Cost per token (net after cache savings): commercial health indicator — high sustained costs reduce margins and can be renewal discussion topic.
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV cache hit %): optimization lever; strong predictor of realized cost reductions and tail latency improvements.

Metric definitions & measurement rules (what to compute and how):
1) Latency — p50 / p95 / p99 request-to-first-token (RTFT):
   - Window: 30-day rolling; compute per-customer and per-route.
   - Units: milliseconds.
   - Exclude: synthetic health checks, requests that error before model start, and outliers > 30s (cap).
   - Tagging: route, model_variant, region.
   - Calculation: for a given customer, aggregate all user requests to the customer’s routes and compute percentiles.

2) Uptime — Customer-Scoped Successful Response Ratio:
   - Window: 7-day rolling for SLO postures; 30-day for QBR summary.
   - Numerator: inference responses with 2xx or 3xx semantics (success or soft-fallback) that returned model output.
   - Denominator: all paid inference requests (excluding retries triggered by client misconfiguration).
   - Presentation: show uptime %, incidents with customer impact, and MTTR (mean time to recovery) per incident.

3) Cost per token — Realized unit cost after cache & batching:
   - Window: billing month (aligned to customer invoicing).
   - Formula (simplified): (Total compute $ charged to customer - cache_savings_$) / (tokens_consumed_after_cache).
   - Notes: show both raw per-token and 90-day trend; annotate major changes (new model variant, quantization, dedicated vs hosted).

4) Cache hit rate — Effective cache utilization:
   - Window: 30-day rolling.
   - Metric: (cached_token_reads) / (total_token_reads) expressed as %; also show prefix-hit % and full-request-hit %.
   - Importance: Converts directly to token savings and lower tail latency for repeated prompts/prompts with long prefix reuse.

Derived KPIs and business translation (how to speak to the customer):
- User Perceived Latency Score (UPLS): normalized 0–100 where p95 latency maps linearly (e.g., <200ms=100, 200–600ms=80–40, >1200ms=0). Use this in QBR charts to show "UX readiness."
- Cost Efficiency Index (CEI): baseline cost_per_token normalized vs platform median for similar workload type (chat, single-shot, embeddings). CEI > 1.2 => discuss optimization plan.
- Reliability Health Index (RHI): uptime weighted with MTTR and incident count. RHI < 92 => escalate to SRE playbook.
- Cache Leverage Factor (CLF): percent token reduction attributable to cache. CLF helps quantify optimization runway.

Suggested KPI table layout (copy this into slide or sheet during a QBR):
Customer: <customer name>
Period: <30-day / billing month>

| KPI                          | Value       | Target          | Trend (30d) | Action if off-target | Owner | Notes |
|------------------------------|-------------|-----------------|-------------|----------------------|-------|-------|
| p95 latency (ms)             | 420         | <300            | ↑20%        | Performance review: add burst capacity / route split | SRE   | LL model updates last week |
| Uptime (%)                   | 99.3        | 99.9 (contract)  | →0.1%       | Root-cause analysis + incident retro | CS/SRE | 1 Sev in window |
| Cost per token ($)           | 0.00085     | <=0.00070       | ↑15%        | Propose quantization + cache tuning | AE/SE | Billing spike on day 10 |
| Cache hit rate (token %)     | 32%         | >=45%           | ↓8%         | Investigate prefix caching config | SE    | Template prompts updated |
| Cache Leverage Factor (CLF)  | 1.18x       | >=1.4x          | ↓         | Improve prompt templates & SDK hints | SE    | |

Scoring heuristic for renewal risk (quick, not formal):
- For a 30-day window compute normalized scores 0–100 for Latency (L), Uptime (U), Cost (C), Cache (H where higher is better).
- Renewal Risk Score (RRS) = 100 - (0.35*L + 0.35*U + 0.2*(100 - C) + 0.1*H)
  - L = UPLS (higher better).
  - U = RHI (higher better).
  - C = CEI mapped so that lower cost gets higher sub-score (inverse normalization).
  - H = CLF normalized.
- Thresholds: RRS > 80 = green, 60–80 = watch, <60 = at-risk.
- Use this as an input into AE prep: attach recent incidents and top 3 ops actions.

Action playbook snippets (trigger-based):
- If p95 latency increases > 30% week-over-week: trigger infra profiling ticket (PRIORITY P2), run hot-path heatmap, consider model_variant downgrade for tail routes, enable short-term dedicated burst.
- If uptime < SLA for >1 day or >3 incidents in 30d: initiate blameless postmortem, prioritize reliability patch, and draft customer incident communication.
- If cost_per_token rises by >20% month-over-month and CEI > 1.2: schedule optimization workshop (quantization, batching policy, cache policy).
- If cache hit rate < target and prefix reuse > 10%: deploy SDK prompt-hinting, update client best-practices, and instrument top 20 prompts for templating.

Customer-facing slide checklist (QBR):
1) One-liner health: RRS and one sentence on why (e.g., "RRS=72: latency and cache drift increased after prompt library change").
2) Two charts: p95 trend and cost-per-token trend.
3) Top incidents & actions (1–3 bullets).
4) Recommended optimization plan and expected impact (est. cost savings / latency improvement).
5) Next steps and owners (AE/SE/SRE).

Appendix: quick formulas to paste into sheet cells:
- p95 latency: =PERCENTILE.INC(range,0.95)
- uptime: =SUM(IF(status_code>=200,1,0))/COUNTA(request_id)
- cost-per-token: =(sum(compute_cost)-cache_savings)/sum(tokens_after_cache)
- cache-hit-rate: =cached_token_reads/total_token_reads

Revision notes:

- 2024-12-13: tuned action thresholds and KPI table (Diego).

How to use this doc:
- Copy KPI table into the QBR deck (slide) and the AE renewal playbook.
- When in doubt, default to the uptime and p95 latency as customer-facing signals; cost conversations happen after technical options are identified.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Formalize CEI baseline cohorts by workload type (chat vs embeddings) — needs product input.
- Add automated query to Console to fetch p95 and cost-per-token per-customer slice for the last invoice period.
